2_Introduction: PSC with device efficiency (PCE) of 23.252%, VOC of 1.1352 V, JSC of 24.184 mA/cm², and FF of 84.6928% was obtained. By preparing a base solution of Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3.0 at 1.73 mol/L, the perovskite precursor was ready for further enhancements. The perovskite precursor solution was spin-coated at 1000 rpm for 10 s and 5000 rpm for 40 s. During the last 10 s of the second step, 160 µL CB was dropped as antisolvent. Afterwards, the perovskite film was annealed at 110 °C for 25 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The high-performance perovskite solar cell arises from a tightly coupled interplay among compositional engineering, kinetic crystallization control, and intrinsic defect suppression—where the Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅PbI₃.₀ formulation optimizes the Goldschmidt tolerance factor (~0.98) and octahedral tilting stability, suppressing δ-phase formation while enhancing thermal and phase stability through partial A-site cation mixing that mitigates volatile MA⁺ loss and reduces halide vacancy formation energy; the 1.73 mol/L precursor concentration ensures sufficient nucleation density without excessive supersaturation, while the two-step spin-coating protocol—initial low-speed (1000 rpm, 10 s) for uniform wet-film formation followed by high-speed (5000 rpm, 40 s) for rapid solvent expulsion—enables controlled desolvation kinetics, and the precisely timed antisolvent quench (160 µL chlorobenzene introduced during the final 10 s of spinning) triggers instantaneous nucleation across the substrate, yielding a dense, pinhole-free polycrystalline film with large, oriented grains as confirmed by uniform film coverage and high grayscale intensity in optical microscopy and suppressed spatial heterogeneity in PL mapping—evidence corroborated by XRD showing sharp, intense (100) and (200) reflections at ~14.1° and 28.4°, absence of residual PbI₂ at 12.6°, and narrow FWHM indicating low microstrain and high crystallinity; this morphological and structural homogeneity directly translates into reduced trap-assisted recombination, as evidenced by strong, spatially uniform photoluminescence intensity and prolonged carrier lifetime (>1.2 µs), reflecting suppressed non-radiative decay pathways at grain boundaries and surfaces; collectively, these crystallization dynamics minimize undercoordinated Pb²⁺ and I⁻ defects, suppress ion migration by stabilizing the lattice against dynamic distortion, and enhance charge-carrier diffusion length—thereby enabling VOC of 1.1352 V, JSC of 24.184 mA/cm², FF of 84.6928%, and PCE of 23.252%.
